name: @layera-labs/video
description: Headless video timeline model + server-side FFmpeg render pipeline for Orbit
author: Layera Labs
//peerDependencies: React is reached ONLY from ./preview-react, which is the one entry that binds the compositor to a component. Optional, because ./preview drives the same canvas with no framework at all and a consumer using it should not be made to install React. Pinned to 18 for the reason the whole repo is: react-konva 18.2.x is the React-18 line, and two React copies is a hard crash in its reconciler rather than a size regression.
//dependencies: @resvg/resvg-js stays a HARD dependency, evaluated rather than assumed (2026-08-09). It is reached only from ./node (raster.ts), so a browser-only consumer installs ~3.4MB of native addon it never loads — resvg distributes its 12 platform binaries as its OWN optionalDependencies, so that is one binary, not twelve, and vite externalizes it while the exports map keeps ./node out of any browser graph. Moving it to optionalDependencies would change NOTHING: an optional dep still installs whenever it can, and is skipped only when its install fails. An optional PEER would genuinely drop it, and that is the option rejected: it turns the render service's install-time resolution into an unenforced runtime contract, and the failure arrives as ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND at import — before any of our code runs, so there is nowhere to say something actionable without restructuring raster.ts and render.ts around a dynamic import. 3.4MB of node_modules disk that is never bundled is the cheaper side of that trade.
//publishConfig: REGISTRY AND ACCESS ARE NOT DECIDED YET, so publishConfig is deliberately absent rather than guessed. Public npm needs {"access":"public"} (a scoped package defaults to restricted and the publish fails without it). GitHub Packages needs {"registry":"https://npm.pkg.github.com"}; the @layera-labs scope already matches the owning GitHub org, so nothing further has to be renamed. Add exactly one of those here before the first publish.
